scores.evidence: 'Morning' section opens on 'If you only caught the last three laps…you saw the pass' — narrative framing before verdict; other sections fare better
'Until next week' paragraph restates standings and previews next race — a textbook summary closer the rule forbids
'At the time it looked like a routine split. It set up the rest of the afternoon.' — bridging sentence between red-flag section and penalty section
'0.85 seconds a lap, taken off a hard tyre that was 40-odd laps old' — good; but '13.7s behind the leader' and '31 seconds' and '18 seconds' cluster in one paragraph
'Would he have won anyway? I don't think so' and 'probably' absent but 'I don't think so' and 'data doesn't carry it' own the speculation cleanly
Russell is the persistent benchmark throughout: tyre age, gap, stop timing, counterfactual — teammate comparison is structural
Track-limits deletion message and Pérez penalty message quoted verbatim as hard evidentiary stops, not decoration
'Leclerc went off on lap 2, race control called SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED' — recaps sequence rather than interpreting; 'Morning' section narrates viewing experience
'Alpine's first pole, second by lap 2, sixth by lap 10, seventh at the flag. No incident anywhere in his trace.' — flat recounting as damning verdict
'I don't think so' appropriately flags judgment; but 'the timing does back up the crowd' is a sentence about the story validating itself
No introductions: Piastri, Lawson, Stroll named and dropped; VSC mechanics assumed; jargon undefined throughout
Almost all paragraphs 2-4 sentences; 'Thirteen seconds' section slightly dense but stays within bounds

'That's 18 seconds cheaper, and 18 seconds is the difference between fresh tyres with time to use them and fresh tyres without. Verstappen pitted at the same moment' — long then short rhythm consistent
VSC mechanism correctly gets the most room; but 'Winners and losers' section runs long on Pérez/Tsunoda marginalia relative to their significance

top_fixes: Kill 'Until next week' entirely — standings and Madrid preview is a summary closer that violates S2 and announces itself as machine-tidy housekeeping; the piece ends when Gasly/Ferrari/Pérez end

Strip the 'Morning' section: 'If you only caught the last three laps…' is a narrative hook addressed to a casual viewer, not peer address; open instead on the sharpest claim about why the race turned where it did

Collapse the Pérez/Tsunoda 'Noted' entry or move the radio verbatim quote earlier as evidentiary punctuation on a claim already made — in its current position it reads like a data-dump footnote rather than a hard stop confirming a reading
